note: Crosswalks indicate substantial overlap, not 1:1 equivalence. See STANDARD.md §9 for context. Boundaries (§9.7) name where OMBS deliberately stops, so an adopter can tell scope adjacency from scope claim. A boundary carries a relation: "distinct-from" is a full boundary — OMBS makes no claim on that framework and does not overlap it. "partial-boundary" concedes a named overlap, carries an acknowledgedOverlap block pointing at the crosswalk that maps it, and bounds only what is left. A partial boundary never means "no relationship", and reading it that way is a misreading of the row.

frameworks.name: Next Generation Science Standards — Engineering Design

mappings.note: Partial, and the closest external match OMBS.S.DG has. 3-5-ETS1-3 asks learners to "Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved" — controlled variables, on an artifact the learner made, to locate what to fix. That is the same cognitive core OMBS.S.DG codes. It is partial in both directions: 3-5-ETS1-3 is a single performance expectation at one grade band, bundled with the ETS1 disciplinary core idea, while OMBS.S.DG spans four bands, assesses no content, and applies in mediums NGSS does not reach. See the ngss-sep-3 boundary for what OMBS does NOT claim.

frameworks.name: P21 / Battelle for Kids — Framework for 21st Century Learning (4Cs)

mappings.note: Partial. Returning to abandoned work and taking it further is one way sustained original work happens; P21 names Creativity at framework level only, so this is mapped no more specifically than the source supports.

Narrowing a fault to the smallest part that still shows it is close observation of parts and relationships. Partial: Agency by Design's triad is about noticing designed systems, not about repairing one's own build.

frameworks.name: CCSS English Language Arts — Writing Standards
Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale (AIAS)
frameworks.note: A five-level scale for the permitted extent of generative-AI use in an assessment task. AIAS states what level of use is ALLOWED; OMBS.S.AI.AB states what the learner must be able to DISCLOSE about the use that occurred. Complementary, not equivalent — an AIAS level is a task rule, not evidence of practice.

mappings.note: AIAS is one of the published disclosure schemes this descriptor accepts.

boundaries.name: UNESCO AI Competency Framework for Students
boundaries.note: OMBS.S.AI and its sub-dimensions assess whether the learner remained the source of choice while making something. They do not assess understanding of AI as subject matter — how models work, where they fail, their societal effects — which is AI literacy and belongs to the UNESCO framework. A tool that reads S.AI as an AI-literacy measure has misread it. See STANDARD.md §1.3 and §4.8.1.

boundaries.name: CASEL Core SEL Competencies
boundaries.note: Critique response, appraisal, and diagnosis are assessed as observable practices on a piece of work, not as dispositions or social-emotional competencies. OMBS.S.DG in particular does not measure persistence, patience, or frustration tolerance: a calm learner who changes five things at once does not satisfy it, and a frustrated learner who changes one thing at a time does. Every S.DG descriptor is decided by a trace on the work — a smaller specimen, a single changed variable, a retained baseline — never by the learner's manner. OMBS.S.RV is at the same risk and is bounded the same way: it does not measure persistence, grit, or follow-through. Abandonment is a legitimate outcome of making, OMBS issues no code for it, and a learner who returns, works, and then sets the piece aside again with a stated reason satisfies OMBS.S.RV in full. What is assessed is the learner's account across the gap, not whether anything was finished. Self-awareness and self-management belong to CASEL. See STANDARD.md §1.3, §4.4 and §9.7.

boundaries.name: NGSS / NRC Framework for K-12 Science Education — Practice 3, Planning and carrying out investigations (as exercised in science-content performance expectations)
boundaries.note: A partial boundary, not a clean separation, and the earlier draft of this row overstated it. Two things must be conceded up front. (1) The NRC Framework places engineering inside Practice 3 itself: "Engineers use investigation both to gain data essential for specifying design criteria or parameters and to test their designs." Practice 3's object is therefore not only a natural phenomenon and its purpose not only scientific knowledge. (2) NGSS applies Practice 3 to a learner's own prototype for the purpose of improving it, in 3-5-ETS1-3 — "Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved." That is OMBS.S.DG's territory, and it is crosswalked as overlapping rather than bounded. What remains bounded is narrower and still worth stating. OMBS.S.DG assesses no disciplinary content: an NGSS performance expectation bundles a practice with a core idea and is satisfied only by demonstrating both, whereas OMBS never asks what the learner knows about any domain. Practice 3's science half — investigating a natural phenomenon to build explanatory knowledge — is outside OMBS.S.DG entirely; OMBS makes no claim on it and is not a substitute for it. And OMBS.S.DG is medium-agnostic across four grade bands: a learner diagnosing why a paragraph loses readers, why a sauce came out flat, or why a scene drags satisfies OMBS.S.DG and no NGSS performance expectation at all. A tool that reads OMBS.S.DG as a science-content measure, or that reads this boundary as denying the 3-5-ETS1-3 overlap, has misread it. See STANDARD.md §1.3, §2.4, §4.4 and §9.7.

acknowledgedOverlap.note: Stated here so this row cannot be read as claiming no relationship. The overlap is real, specific, and separately crosswalked.
